title: Permitting Connections Before Application Bootstrapping Completes
pattern: A server binds to a socket and starts accepting incoming client connections *before* the underlying application components (like database connection pools or repositories) are fully initialized.
why_bad: Clients can submit requests that immediately crash or hang because the backing storage engine or configuration is still uninitialized.
detection: Network listening or listener thread spawning occurs before application-level dependency injection, configuration parsing, or database pool initialization.
counterexample: A gateway server that safely buffers incoming connections in a queue until the worker pool signals readiness.
fix: Fully initialize all internal application services and pools before binding to the network socket and flipping the "master switch" to accept client traffic.
